newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell spinoff to be cautious on acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell spinoff to be cautious on acquisitions.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp's soon-to-be-spun-off automotive unit Thursday unveiled a new name and a charging winged bull logo but said it will remain cautious about acquisitions.
The 90-year-old manufacturer of heavy truck axles, car sunroofs and door modules and other components, with 1996 sales of $3.1 billion, said it will be adopt the name Meritor Automotive Inc.
Under its spinoff agreement with Rockwell, Meritor agreed to change its corporate name but it will still be able to use the Rockwell name on its products for up to 10 years.

On September 30, Rockwell shareholders will receive one share of Meritor for every three Rockwell shares they own. Rockwell will continue as an electronics company focused on its avionics, industrial automation and semiconductor businesses.

Meritor's stock will begin trading under a new symbol on the New York Stock Exchange on October 1, but Chief Financial Officer Thomas Madden said the Troy, Mich.-based company does not expect to use the new shares as acquisition currency for a few years.

"We're not going to jump into the acquisition market right away," Madden told reporters at a news conference here. He added that Meritor wants to ensure that it maintain its focus on serving its customers.
However, if the right opportunity came along at the right price, the company would seriously consider making a cash acquisition, he said, adding "We have plenty of financial firepower."

After paying a $400 million dividend back to Rockwell, Meritor will start out with $50 million to $100 million in cash and a $1 billion line of credit provided by a consortium of 18 banks, led by First Chicago-NBD Corp, Madden said.

He declined to project the company's sales for fiscal 1997, which ends September 30, but said the company's average annual capital expenditures of about $120 million over the past five years would continue at at least the same level.

Meritor will remain in Rockwell Automotive's Troy, Mich., headquarters and technical center, where it employs about 800 people. Rockwell Automotive President Larry Yost, who will become chairman of the new company, said he expects the headquarters staff to expand by about 50 people.
Meritor employs more than 16,000 people at 58 plants, research and sales facilities plants in 15 countries.
Yost said the new name was derived from the Latin word "meritum," meaning service, worth and benefit.
"The Meritor name and logo symbolize the quality, integrity, experience, longevity and outstanding service that are the core attributes of our enterprise," he added.

He said the bull is a "mythical" symbol of power, stability integrity and agility. Asked if it was Greek or Roman mythology, he said it was "Landor mythology," a reference to Landor Associates, the corporate identity firm that came up with the name and logo.
The logo also includes the phrase "A heritage of Rockwell technology," to create a link to the company's past.
